A_general.open_code_note: The official microsoft/mcp repository contains a separately documented, local-first Fabric MCP server. Microsoft distinguishes it from the hosted Core endpoint: the local server runs as a subprocess and includes documentation, OneLake, core, and Data Factory tools. Its tools are not included in this endpoint's action list. The repository archive was not available in the evidence folder, so its implementation was not analyzed locally.
A_general.license: N/A (hosted implementation is closed; the separate local repository is not the deployed server)
other_official_servers: Microsoft documents a separate local Fabric MCP Server for API documentation, OneLake, core Fabric, and Data Factory workflows. It is not the input endpoint. https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/fabric/articles/mcp-servers/pro-dev-local/overview-local-mcp-server

Microsoft's Fabric server directory lists other hosted workload-specific servers, including Data Warehouse, Eventhouse, Activator, Operations agent, Fabric IQ, and Power BI Authoring. These are distinct servers with separate documentation and tool sets. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/fabric/articles/mcp-servers/fabric-mcp-servers-list

Microsoft Graph MCP is a separate server that the Core setup guide says can resolve user and group identities by email for permission operations. https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/fabric/articles/mcp-servers/core-remote/get-started-core

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: The reviewed Microsoft materials do not state a separate fee for connecting to or calling the Core MCP endpoint. They require a Fabric tenant, an Entra ID account with Fabric permissions, and suitable Fabric access. Charges for underlying Fabric capacity may apply.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Fabric capacity is offered pay-as-you-go or by reservation; Microsoft also advertises a free trial. The pricing page's rendered price values were placeholders, so no numeric amount is reported.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Fabric capacity pricing is based on Capacity Units and capacity SKU; Microsoft describes pay-as-you-go, reservation, a one-minute minimum, and possible overage charges. No MCP-specific per-call price, quota, or credit cost was found.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Requires an active Fabric tenant, an MCP host supporting Streamable HTTP and the Microsoft Entra ID flow, and an account with Fabric permissions. Workspace creation can be restricted by organization roles. The documentation does not identify an endpoint-specific client allowlist, beta flag, or rate limit.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Microsoft controls endpoint availability and the OAuth resource; organization administrators and Fabric RBAC determine tenant and user permissions; the MCP host controls its own transport/authentication support and approval settings.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: Microsoft's official Core tools reference names 29 tools covering catalog search; workspaces and workspace roles; items and item definitions; bulk item movement; folders; capacities; operation status and results; and item-type guidance. It says each tool maps to a Fabric REST API operation and includes input validation and error handling. The reference does not publish input schemas or annotations.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Tool-specific result and error schemas are NOT FOUND in the available official reference. The endpoint's unauthenticated response was HTTP 401 with JSON errorCode TokenIsMissing, message Access token is required, and isRetriable false.

The setup and tools documentation provides example user prompts, but does not state that the server implements MCP prompts or expose prompt definitions.

Microsoft says Fabric records supported Core operations in audit logs under the identity that executes the operation. Documentation does not specify that every MCP tool call is logged, nor describe MCP-specific diagnostic or telemetry fields.

C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Fabric audit events for supported operations; exact event coverage and event fields are not specified in the Core MCP overview.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official list includes read operations and state-changing operations, including workspace/item/folder deletion and workspace-role grant, update, and removal. The reference publishes no readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, or openWorldHint annotations. 2. No server-enforced confirmation parameter, preview/confirm sequence, or elicitation is documented. Microsoft recommends client-side approval review; workspace deletion is described as permanent and irreversible, and folder deletion requires an empty folder. 3. OAuth uses Microsoft Entra ID and the supplied protected-resource metadata lists https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/.default. Operations inherit the authenticated identity's Fabric permissions. Workspace creation may be restricted by organization role. DCR, PKCE, token lifetime/revocation, and client allowlists are Unknown. 4. No read-only endpoint, toolset filter, query-free mode, sandbox/production split, or region-specific Core endpoint was found in reviewed docs. Other Fabric MCP servers are separately listed. 5. No MCP-specific PII masking or field exclusion is documented. Workspace permissions constrain accessible resources; Microsoft says resource-management tools are not general-purpose table query/modification tools. 6. No endpoint-specific quota, rate limit, bulk cap, or truncation policy was found. Underlying Fabric capacity may incur capacity charges. 7. The tools reference says tools include input validation and error handling, but schemas, rejection policy, coercions, and parameter correction are not published. 8. Microsoft says supported Core operations are recorded in Fabric audit logs under the executing identity; exact event coverage and MCP telemetry are not specified. 9. The 29 official tool names contain no feedback, rating, survey, report, or marketing tool. No MCP upsell result or product-preference instruction was found. 10. No hosted server instructions or skills are published. Documentation guidance recommending least privilege and client approvals is not documented as server-enforced. 11. No memory or behavior-dependent capability is documented. 12. The documented Core server is a flat remote tool surface mapping tools to Fabric REST operations. Other workload servers and the local Fabric server are separate endpoints/variants. No nested AI-agent tool is documented. 13. No raw API request, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or universal escape-hatch tool appears in the official Core list.

Microsoft's local server and workload-specific servers are separate products/endpoints, not documented as dynamically loaded subservers of this endpoint.

All 29 names are listed in actions.json. No catalogue-only actions were added. The GitHub MCP Registry page points to Microsoft's separate local Fabric server, not the hosted Core endpoint. The ZBS catalogue reports its isolated package probe exited before returning tools, so it supplies no action names. F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Microsoft advises operators to review tool calls and client approval settings before changes, apply least-privilege RBAC, and use the correct workspace UUID. The docs do not say these safeguards are enforced by the server. Verbatim: "Review agent-generated tool calls and your client's approval settings before allowing changes." and "Use the workspace ID (UUID format) in subsequent operations."
F_documentation.governance_promises: Microsoft documents that operations use the authenticated identity's Fabric permissions and that supported operations are recorded in Fabric audit logs under the executing identity. It warns that clients may perform destructive actions and states workspace deletion permanently removes contained items. It also places responsibility for client/service data handling and compliance on the user. No MCP-specific promises about data retention, AI training, masking, or telemetry were found.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Microsoft describes typed tool operations with input validation and error handling, and says the authenticated identity's Fabric permissions apply. It says resource-management tools do not provide general-purpose lakehouse-table querying or modification.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The hosted implementation is closed, so enforcement details could not be verified in code. Documentation says permissions apply and supported operations are audited, but does not specify audit coverage or enforcement internals. Client approval and least-privilege are recommendations, not documented server-enforced confirmation gates. The tool list includes destructive operations, consistent with the documented warning that clients can invoke them.

observations_for_research: The endpoint advertises a single OAuth .default scope for the Fabric API resource; the supplied metadata does not expose granular MCP-specific scopes, while the documentation describes authorization as inherited Fabric RBAC.

The official tool reference names every action but does not publish tool input schemas or MCP annotations, so parameter-level comparison and exact pre-interaction context sizing are not possible from the available official evidence.
The docs describe permanent workspace deletion and client-side review safeguards but do not document a server-side confirmation gate.
